deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page derives displacements and stresses (N_i normal, T_i shear stresses) of an isotropic elastic body with Lamé constants λ, μ under a point force, and lists image positions (-a-ξ, -ξ, ξ, a-ξ, 2a+ξ, ...) for a slab -a/2<x<a/2. On this page Riemann does two things. (A) He writes the point-force field in a form suited to a rectangular box. (B) He evaluates the triply periodic image sums that this requires, using the Gaussian (Mellin) representation of 1/ρ and the theta transformation. The right half is a side study of the Jacobi theta function. The theta part supports (B).

(A) Elastic field. Take ρ² = (x-ξ)²+(y-η)²+(z-ζ)² and (my reading) φ = ρ. Riemann writes
 u = (λ+μ) ∂²φ/∂x² - 2(λ+2μ)/ρ,
 v = (λ+μ) ∂²φ/∂x∂y,
 w = (λ+μ) ∂²φ/∂x∂z.
This uses ∂i∂jρ = δij/ρ - (xi-ξi)(xj-ξj)/ρ³. Up to an overall factor it is -[2(λ+2μ)δij/ρ - (λ+μ)∂i∂jρ], which equals -[(λ+3μ)δij/ρ + (λ+μ)xi xj/ρ³]. That is Kelvin's 1848 fundamental solution for a force in the x-direction, so the Navier equations μΔu+(λ+μ)∇(div u)=0 hold away from the source.

Next come correction terms in brackets, multiplied by 2(λ+mu). These are ma ∂(1/ρ)/∂x + nb ∫∂²(1/ρ)/∂x² dy + pc ∫∂²(1/ρ)/∂x² dz, with analogous terms for v and w. They arise because translated or reflected images carry a factor (x-ξ) that shifts by ma, nb, pc (cf. the '+na·4(λ+μ)...' list on the previous page). A third column adds (λ+μ)((y-η)∂²(1/ρ)/∂x² dy - ∂(1/ρ)/∂x)-type terms; these are only partly legible.

The image lattice is declared as (ξ+2ma, η+2nb, ζ+2pc), together with reflected images. So both Σ±1/ρ and Σ±ρ (for φ) over the lattice are needed.

(B) Lattice sums.
(1) Riemann writes ∫_0^∞ e^{-ρ² s} s^{-1/2} ds = Π(-1/2)/ρ, where Π(-1/2) = Γ(1/2) = √π. Hence
 Σ(-1)^{m+n+p}/ρ_{mnp} = (1/Π(-1/2)) ∫_0^∞ s^{-1/2} Σ(-1)^{m+n+p} e^{-sρ²} ds.
The Gaussian factorizes into a product of three one-dimensional sums Σ_m (-1)^m e^{-s(x-ξ-ma)²} · Σ_n · Σ_p.
(2) Likewise Σ(-1)^{m+n+p} ρ = (1/Π(-3/2)) ∫_0^∞ s^{-3/2} (...) ds, with Π(-3/2) = Γ(-1/2) = -2√π. Strictly this needs the subtraction e^{-sρ²}-1, which the alternating signs supply in the sum.
(3) For the box he writes the image sum per coordinate as Σ_m 1/√((x-ξ+2ma)²+...) + Σ_m 1/√((x+ξ-(2m+1)a)²+...). The images are reflections in the planes x = ±a/2 + ma, i.e. the box -a/2<x<a/2.
(4) Theta transformation (right half, bottom). Put q = e^{-4a²s} (his '-log q = 4aas') and Ξ = e^{4as(x-ξ)} (his 'log ξ = 4as(x-ξ)'). Then
 Σ_m e^{-s(x-ξ-2ma)²} = e^{-s(x-ξ)²} Σ q^{m²} Ξ^m = √(π/(4a²s)) Σ_m e^{-π²m²/(4a²s) - mπi(x-ξ)/a}.
This is the Poisson/Jacobi transformation and is exactly his last line.
(5) Adding the direct and reflected series gives, per coordinate,
 cos(mπ(x-ξ)/a) + cos(mπ(x+ξ-a)/a) = 2 cos mπ(x/a-1/2) cos mπ(ξ/a-1/2).
He also has a struck variant with sin mπx/a sin mπξ/a, the Dirichlet / sign-alternating case on (0,a).
(6) The three factors √(π/(4a²s)) etc. combine with s^{-1/2} to give s^{-2}. With A = (π²/4)(m²/a²+n²/b²+p²/c²),
 ∫_0^∞ s^{-2} e^{-A/s} ds = 1/A.
This yields the eigenfunction (Fourier) expansion
 Σ images 1/ρ = const·(1/abc) Σ_{m,n,p} Π[cos mπ(x/a-1/2) cos mπ(ξ/a-1/2)] / [(π²/4)(m²/a²+n²/b²+p²/c²)].
This is the box Green's function as a triple Fourier series, derived from the image sum. The constant is the 8 he writes, with 1/Π(-1/2)^3-type factors.
(7) Auxiliary: ∫_0^1 x^{-1/2}(1-x)^{-1/2} dx = Π(-1/2)² = π.

Right half: theta function study.
- With q = e^{-π²/χ}, he writes terms e^{-π²n²/χ + nπui/(2χ)} and θ(q) = 1+2q+2q⁴+2q⁹+... ≈ √(2χ/π). The intended content is the leading term of the theta transformation as q→1.
- Product form (Jacobi triple product): (1+qΞ)(1+q³Ξ)...(1+q/Ξ)(1+q³/Ξ)...
- Series Θ(Ξ) = Σ q^{n²} Ξ^n = ... + q⁴/Ξ² + q/Ξ + 1 + qΞ + q⁴Ξ² + ...
- Quasi-periodicity Θ(q²Ξ) = Θ(Ξ)/(qΞ), checked by writing out Σ q^{n²+2n} Ξ^n = Ξ^{-2} + q^{-1}Ξ^{-1} + 1 + q³Ξ + q⁸Ξ² + ...
- Zeros: log Ξ = (2n+1) log q + (2m+1)πi.
- Modular relation: log q' = π²/log q.
These are used to justify the transformation in (4).
errors: '√(2χ/π) = 1+2q+2q⁴+...' with q=e^{-π²/χ}: Jacobi's transformation gives Σq^{n²} = √(χ/π)·Σe^{-χk²} ≈ √(χ/π) as χ→∞. The factor 2 under the root looks like a slip or a different normalization of χ (or a misreading).

Σ(-1)^{m+n+p}ρ = (1/Π(-3/2))∫ s^{-3/2}Σ(...)ds is only valid after regularization: ∫_0^∞ s^{-3/2}e^{-sρ²}ds diverges at s=0. One needs (e^{-sρ²}-1), which the alternating sum effectively provides. This is unstated.
Interchanging the conditionally convergent alternating 3D sum with the s-integral is unjustified as written, though standard and correct in the end (Ewald-type regularization).

In the non-alternating (Neumann-type, cos·cos) case the m=n=p=0 term has A=0 and diverges. The pure-Neumann box Green's function does not exist without removing the zero mode; the page does not address this.

The overall constant (8/abc vs π/abc summed over all integer triples) cannot be confirmed from the image. A direct check gives Σ_images 1/ρ = (π/abc) Σ_{k∈Z³} Πcos·cos / A, with A=(π²/4)(m²/a²+n²/b²+p²/c²).
Notation clash: ξ is used both for the source coordinate and the theta variable (log ξ = 4as(x-ξ)).

results.what: Point-force displacement in an isotropic elastic solid: u_i ∝ 2(λ+2μ)δ_ij/ρ - (λ+μ)∂_i∂_jρ
1/ρ = (1/√π)∫_0^∞ s^{-1/2}e^{-sρ²}ds; ρ via Γ(-1/2); factorization of a 3D lattice sum into products of 1D Gaussian sums
results.modern_name: Mellin/Gaussian (heat-kernel) representation of Coulomb lattice sums
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1859 (zeta paper) for the 1D case; Epstein 1903, Ewald 1921 for 3D lattices

results.what: Method of images in a rectangular box converted, via the theta transformation and ∫s^{-2}e^{-A/s}ds = 1/A, into the triple Fourier eigenfunction expansion of the Green's function, with denominators π²/4(m²/a²+n²/b²+p²/c²)
results.modern_name: Image-sum ↔ eigenfunction-expansion equivalence for the box Green's function (Ewald-type summation of alternating lattice potentials, cf. Madelung sum Σ(-1)^{m+n+p}/ρ)
results.usually_credited_to: Eigenfunction expansions: Fourier/Poisson era; lattice-sum version: Madelung 1918, Ewald 1921

results.what: Jacobi triple product form of θ, quasi-periodicity Θ(q²Ξ)=Θ(Ξ)/(qΞ), zeros at Ξ=-q^{2n+1}, modular relation log q·log q' = π²
results.modern_name: Jacobi theta function identities (triple product, quasi-periodicity, imaginary transformation)

deep.surprise_reason: Each ingredient is classical and very much in Riemann's style: the Gaussian/theta trick from the 1859 zeta paper and images from his PDE lectures. Applying it to a 3D alternating Coulomb lattice sum and a box Green's function for elasticity anticipates the Madelung/Ewald lattice-sum technique (1918–21). That makes it a notable unpublished application, though not a new theorem.

transcription_corrections: Third line, right column: '+λμ((y-η)...)' should read '+(λ+μ)((y-η)...)', and '∂φ/∂x∂z' should be '∂²φ/∂x∂z'.
'1+q 3/ξ (1+q^5 ξ)' should be '(1+q³/ξ)(1+q⁵ξ)' (factors of the triple product).
'1/ξ q⁴ + 1/ξ q + 1 + qξ + q⁴ξ² + ... = 0' should read 'q⁴/ξ² + q/ξ + 1 + qξ + q⁴ξ² + ...' (the series Θ(ξ)); likewise the next line is 'ξ^{-2} + q^{-1}ξ^{-1} + 1 + q³ξ + q⁸ξ²', i.e. Θ(q²ξ).
'ξ + qξ' near Θ(q²ξ) is probably 'ξ → q²ξ' (the substitution).
The symbol before '(ξ+2ma, η+2nb, ζ+2pc), ρ=0' is a struck Σ/abbreviation naming the image-point lattice (poles where ρ=0).
'4 cos mπ(x/a-1/2) cos mπ(ξ/a-1/2) ∂s/ss' — the ∂s/ss (= ds/s²) belongs to the s-integral, consistent with s^{-1/2}·s^{-3/2}.
